---
title: "23 — AI/AN expanded-feature multilayer perceptron (MLP) in R"
subtitle: "2023 training and tuning | 2024 recalibration | 2025 exploratory evaluation"
output: html_notebook
---

## Purpose

**Question:** Can a small, regularized neural network improve frequent mental distress (FMD) classification among AI/AN-alone respondents compared with Notebook 21 (logistic, LASSO, random forest) and Notebook 22 (XGBoost)?

This notebook uses **R `torch` only**, not Python. It does not modify other notebooks or their outputs.

- **2023:** Same source, 25 prespecified predictor groups and encoding as Notebooks 21–22. Choose among three small MLPs using a reproducible stratified 80/20 split *inside 2023*, validation weighted Brier score, and early stopping. Refit the selected architecture for its selected epoch count on **all eligible 2023 respondents**.
- **2024:** Audit raw generalization and apply *intercept-only* probability recalibration based on 2024 survey-weighted observed FMD prevalence.
- **2025:** Evaluate frozen model with AUROC, Brier, mean predicted vs observed, calibration, ROC, confusion matrices (0.16, 0.20, and 0.50), and classifications. Optional comparison reads 21/22 results only if sample/source checks agree.

**Boundaries:** FMD is contemporaneous with the predictors (especially physically unhealthy days); this is **not** a prediction of future events or individual suicide risk. The dataset is a supplied AI/AN-alone subset, not independently verified Tribal affiliation. BRFSS survey weights are used as *pseudo-weights* for fitting and to calculate descriptive evaluation metrics; this notebook **does not estimate full complex-survey variances or confidence intervals**. Since 2025 outcomes were examined in earlier notebooks, the 2025 comparisons are **exploratory/post-hoc**. The within-2023 holdout shares predictor preprocessing fitted on all 2023 records; its Brier score is a tuning diagnostic, not an independent estimate of generalization.

### Install the R packages first (run in the Console once)

```r
install.packages(c("torch", "data.table", "ggplot2", "scales"))
torch::install_torch() # installs LibTorch/LibLantern if needed
# Restart R if prompted. CPU execution is supported; no Python needed.
```

Official documentation: [R torch installation](https://torch.mlverse.org/docs/articles/installation) and [binary cross-entropy with logits](https://torch.mlverse.org/docs/reference/nnf_binary_cross_entropy_with_logits.html).

```{r setup}
weighted_mean_23 <- function(x, w) {
  keep <- !is.na(x) & is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
  if (!any(keep)) return(NA_real_)
  sum(x[keep] * w[keep]) / sum(w[keep])
}
```

## 2 — Prespecified feature dictionary and training-year coverage

Same coding decisions as Notebook 21/22. Valid BRFSS categories are treated as categorical factors; refused/unknown responses are missing, not numeric severity scores. Depression diagnoses, mental-health outcome variables, alcohol and substance use, race, geography, and weight are **excluded as predictors**. Only predictors present and sufficiently observed in 2023 are retained.

```{r feature-dictionary}
feature_23 <- function(source, label, domain, allowed, kind = "categorical") {
  list(source = source, label = label, domain = domain,
       allowed = allowed, kind = kind)
}
feature_specs <- list(
  feature_23("GENHLTH", "General health", "Physical health", 1:5),
  feature_23("PHYSHLTH", "Physically unhealthy days", "Physical health", 0:30, "days"),
  feature_23("_AGEG5YR", "Age group", "Demographics", 1:13),
  feature_23("SEXVAR", "Sex", "Demographics", 1:2),
  feature_23("EDUCA", "Education", "Socioeconomic", 1:6),
  feature_23("INCOME3", "Household income", "Socioeconomic", 1:11),
  feature_23("EMPLOY1", "Employment", "Socioeconomic", 1:8),
  feature_23("RENTHOM1", "Home tenure", "Socioeconomic", 1:3),
  feature_23("PERSDOC3", "Has personal healthcare provider", "Healthcare access", 1:3),
  feature_23("MEDCOST1", "Could not afford medical care", "Healthcare access", 1:2),
  feature_23("CHECKUP1", "Time since routine checkup", "Healthcare access", c(1:4, 8)),
  feature_23("EXERANY2", "Exercise in past 30 days", "Health activity", 1:2),
  feature_23("DIFFWALK", "Difficulty walking", "Functional health", 1:2),
  feature_23("DIFFDRES", "Difficulty dressing", "Functional health", 1:2),
  feature_23("DIFFALON", "Difficulty doing errands alone", "Functional health", 1:2),
  feature_23("DEAF", "Deaf or serious hearing difficulty", "Functional health", 1:2),
  feature_23("BLIND", "Blind or serious visual difficulty", "Functional health", 1:2),
  feature_23("ASTHMA3", "Ever diagnosed with asthma", "Chronic conditions", 1:2),
  feature_23("CVDINFR4", "Heart attack history", "Chronic conditions", 1:2),
  feature_23("CVDCRHD4", "Coronary heart disease history", "Chronic conditions", 1:2),
  feature_23("CVDSTRK3", "Stroke history", "Chronic conditions", 1:2),
  feature_23("CHCCOPD3", "COPD history", "Chronic conditions", 1:2),
  feature_23("CHCKDNY2", "Kidney disease history", "Chronic conditions", 1:2),
  feature_23("HAVARTH4", "Arthritis history", "Chronic conditions", 1:2),
  feature_23("DIABETE4", "Diabetes status", "Chronic conditions", 1:4)

clean_feature_23 <- function(d, s) {
  if (!(s$source %in% names(d))) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(d)))
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d[[s$source]]))
  if (identical(s$kind, "days")) {
    x[!is.na(x) & x == 88] <- 0
  }
  x[is.na(x) | !(x %in% s$allowed)] <- NA_real_
  x
}
# Readable safe column names, with raw BRFSS codes recorded separately.
feat_names <- make.names(vapply(feature_specs, `[[`, "", "label"), unique = TRUE)
feature_dictionary <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(feature_specs), function(i) {
  s <- feature_specs[[i]]
  data.table::data.table(source = s$source, feature = s$label,
    encoded_name = feat_names[i], domain = s$domain, kind = s$kind,
    allowed_codes = paste(s$allowed, collapse = ","), exists = s$source %in% names(raw))
}))
write_table_23(feature_dictionary, "23_feature_dictionary")
print(feature_dictionary)

original_values <- lapply(feature_specs, function(s) clean_feature_23(raw, s))
coverage <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(feature_specs), function(i) {
  data.table::data.table(
    YEAR = raw$YEAR, observed = !is.na(original_values[[i]])
  )[, .(valid_n = sum(observed), records = .N,
         coverage_pct = 100 * mean(observed)), by = YEAR][,
      `:=`(source = feature_specs[[i]]$source,
           feature = feature_specs[[i]]$label,
           encoded_name = feat_names[i])]
}))
write_table_23(coverage, "23_feature_coverage_by_year")
training_coverage <- coverage[YEAR == 2023L]
training_coverage[, training_distinct_codes := vapply(source,
  function(src) {
    i <- match(src, vapply(feature_specs, `[[`, "", "source"))
    data.table::uniqueN(original_values[[i]][raw$YEAR == 2023L], na.rm = TRUE)
  }, integer(1))]
training_coverage[, retained := coverage_pct >= 75 & training_distinct_codes >= 2]
training_coverage[, reason := ifelse(retained, "Retained",
  "Less than 75% valid in 2023 or fewer than 2 observed codes")]
write_table_23(training_coverage, "23_2023_feature_selection")
print(training_coverage[, .(source, feature, coverage_pct, training_distinct_codes, retained)])

selected_indices <- which(training_coverage$retained)
# 2023 model fitting must retain the original six domains at minimum.
core_sources <- c("GENHLTH", "PHYSHLTH", "_AGEG5YR", "SEXVAR", "EDUCA", "INCOME3")
if (!all(core_sources %in% feature_dictionary$source[selected_indices])) {
  stop("Missing a core source predictor. Review 2023 feature coding and coverage.")
}
selected_specs <- feature_specs[selected_indices]
selected_names <- feat_names[selected_indices]
cat("[FEATURE SELECTION]", length(selected_specs), "of", length(feature_specs),
    "prespecified predictor groups retained.\n")
```

## 3 — Encode and impute without using 2024/2025 outcomes

Same 2023 median/mode imputation, factor levels, and one-hot encoding as Notebook 21/22. The model matrix must match across years. One-hot columns retain their 0/1 values; physically unhealthy days are standardized using the 2023 mean and SD.

```{r prepare-features}
analysis <- data.table::copy(raw[, .(YEAR, RAW_WEIGHT, FMD)])
training_mask <- raw$YEAR == 2023L
most_common_23 <- function(x) {
  v <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(v)) stop("No observed training values for a selected feature.")
  as.numeric(names(sort(table(v), decreasing = TRUE)[1L]))
}
preprocess_params <- list()
missing_audit <- list()
for (j in seq_along(selected_indices)) {
  idx <- selected_indices[j]
  s <- feature_specs[[idx]]
  nm <- feat_names[idx]
  x <- original_values[[idx]]
  x_train <- x[training_mask]
  train_levels <- sort(unique(x_train[!is.na(x_train)]))
  replacement <- if (identical(s$kind, "days")) {
    stats::median(x_train, na.rm = TRUE)
  } else most_common_23(x_train)
  was_missing <- is.na(x)
  was_unseen <- !is.na(x) & !(x %in% train_levels)
  x[was_missing | was_unseen] <- replacement

  if (identical(s$kind, "days")) {
    mu <- mean(x[training_mask])
    sigma <- stats::sd(x[training_mask])
    if (!is.finite(sigma) || sigma <= 0) stop("Zero/invalid training SD for ", nm)
    x_final <- pmax(-3, pmin(3, (x - mu) / sigma))
  } else {
    mu <- NA_real_
    sigma <- NA_real_
    x_final <- factor(paste0("code_", x), levels = paste0("code_", train_levels))
  }
  analysis[, (nm) := x_final]
  preprocess_params[[nm]] <- list(source = s$source, kind = s$kind,
    train_levels = train_levels, replacement = replacement,
    mean_2023 = mu, sd_2023 = sigma)
  missing_audit[[j]] <- data.table::data.table(
    YEAR = sort(unique(raw$YEAR)), feature = s$label, source = s$source,
    originally_missing_n = vapply(sort(unique(raw$YEAR)), function(yr)
      sum(was_missing[raw$YEAR == yr]), integer(1)),
    unseen_code_n = vapply(sort(unique(raw$YEAR)), function(yr)
      sum(was_unseen[raw$YEAR == yr]), integer(1))
  )
}
write_table_23(data.table::rbindlist(missing_audit), "23_imputation_and_unseen_codes")

# Restrict all three models and both evaluation years to valid binary FMD outcomes.
train <- analysis[YEAR == 2023L & !is.na(FMD)]
valid <- analysis[YEAR == 2024L & !is.na(FMD)]
test <- analysis[YEAR == 2025L & !is.na(FMD)]
for (d in list(train, valid, test)) {
  if (!identical(sort(unique(d$FMD)), 0:1)) stop("An analysis year lacks an outcome class.")
}
get_features <- function(d) as.data.frame(d[, ..selected_names])
train_df <- get_features(train)
valid_df <- get_features(valid)
test_df <- get_features(test)

# Identical model-matrix columns across years, derived from 2023 factor levels.
mm_formula <- stats::as.formula("~ .")
model_matrix <- function(df) {
  m <- stats::model.matrix(mm_formula, data = df)
  m <- m[, colnames(m) != "(Intercept)", drop = FALSE]
  storage.mode(m) <- "double"
  m
}
X_train <- model_matrix(train_df)
X_valid <- model_matrix(valid_df)
X_test <- model_matrix(test_df)
if (!identical(colnames(X_train), colnames(X_valid)) ||
    !identical(colnames(X_train), colnames(X_test))) {
  stop("Model matrix columns differ across years; check factor levels.")
}
if (!all(is.finite(X_train)) || !all(is.finite(X_valid)) || !all(is.finite(X_test))) {
  stop("Unexpected missing or invalid encoded predictors.")
}
# Survey pseudo-weights, normalized to have mean 1 within each year's outcome sample.
scale_weights_23 <- function(w) w / mean(w)
train_weights <- scale_weights_23(train$RAW_WEIGHT)
valid_weights <- scale_weights_23(valid$RAW_WEIGHT)

sample_counts <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(list(train=train, valid=valid, test=test), function(d) {
  data.table::data.table(n = nrow(d), FMD_n = sum(d$FMD == 1L),
    prevalence_pct = 100 * weighted_mean_23(d$FMD, d$RAW_WEIGHT),
    effective_n_kish = sum(d$RAW_WEIGHT)^2 / sum(d$RAW_WEIGHT^2))
}), idcol = "split")
write_table_23(sample_counts, "23_modeling_samples")
print(sample_counts)
cat("[ENCODED]", ncol(X_train), "model-matrix columns for",
    length(selected_specs), "predictor groups.\n")
```

## 4 — A small MLP with dropout and weighted BCE loss

The network uses **two hidden ReLU layers**, dropout between layers, and **one output logit** for binary FMD classification. Apply sigmoid only when converting logits to probabilities. The training objective uses weighted binary cross-entropy, normalized by the sum of weights in each mini-batch. Class imbalance is *not* automatically reweighted, because a balanced-class loss would distort prevalence probabilities. Weight decay, small hidden layers, and early stopping limit overfitting.

```{r define-mlp}
torch::torch_manual_seed(2301L)
# CPU works across computers and avoids GPU-specific installation issues.
mlp_device <- torch::torch_device("cpu")
mlp_23 <- torch::nn_module(
  "FMD_MLP_23",
  initialize = function(input_dim, hidden1, hidden2, dropout) {
    self$network <- torch::nn_sequential(
      torch::nn_linear(input_dim, hidden1),
      torch::nn_relu(),
      torch::nn_dropout(p = dropout),
      torch::nn_linear(hidden1, hidden2),
      torch::nn_relu(),
      torch::nn_dropout(p = dropout),
      torch::nn_linear(hidden2, 1L)
    )
  },
  forward = function(x) {
    # (batch, 1) -> (batch) so targets and sample weights share shape.
    self$network(x)$squeeze(2)
  }
)

predict_mlp_23 <- function(model, X, batch_size = 1024L) {
  model$eval()  # disable dropout
  p <- numeric(nrow(X))
  torch::with_no_grad({
    for (start in seq.int(1L, nrow(X), by = batch_size)) {
      idx <- start:min(nrow(X), start + batch_size - 1L)
      tensor_x <- torch::torch_tensor(X[idx, , drop = FALSE],
                                      dtype = torch::torch_float(), device = mlp_device)
      logits <- model(tensor_x)
      p[idx] <- as.numeric(as.array(torch::torch_sigmoid(logits)$cpu()))
    }
  })
  if (any(!is.finite(p)) || length(p) != nrow(X)) stop("MLP predictions are invalid.")
  pmax(1e-6, pmin(1 - 1e-6, p))
}

fit_mlp_23 <- function(X, y, w, config, max_epochs, seed,
                       X_holdout = NULL, y_holdout = NULL, w_holdout = NULL,
                       early_stopping = FALSE, patience = 16L, batch_size = 256L) {
  stopifnot(nrow(X) == length(y), length(y) == length(w), all(w > 0))
  set.seed(as.integer(seed))
  torch::torch_manual_seed(as.integer(seed))
  model <- mlp_23(input_dim = ncol(X), hidden1 = as.integer(config$hidden1),
    hidden2 = as.integer(config$hidden2), dropout = config$dropout)
  model$to(device = mlp_device)
  optimizer <- torch::optim_adamw(model$parameters, lr = config$learning_rate,
                                   weight_decay = config$weight_decay)
  history <- vector("list", max_epochs)
  best_epoch <- 1L
  best_holdout <- Inf
  epochs_without_gain <- 0L
  # Final training uses the epoch count selected before observing 2024/2025.
  for (epoch in seq_len(max_epochs)) {
    model$train()
    shuffled <- sample.int(nrow(X))
    batch_losses <- numeric(0)
    for (start in seq.int(1L, length(shuffled), by = batch_size)) {
      rows <- shuffled[start:min(length(shuffled), start + batch_size - 1L)]
      xb <- torch::torch_tensor(X[rows, , drop = FALSE],
                                dtype = torch::torch_float(), device = mlp_device)
      yb <- torch::torch_tensor(as.numeric(y[rows]),
                                dtype = torch::torch_float(), device = mlp_device)
      wb <- torch::torch_tensor(as.numeric(w[rows]),
                                dtype = torch::torch_float(), device = mlp_device)
      optimizer$zero_grad()
      logits <- model(xb)
      per_case_loss <- torch::nnf_binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
        logits, yb, reduction = "none")
      loss <- (per_case_loss * wb)$sum() / wb$sum()
      loss$backward()
      optimizer$step()
      batch_losses <- c(batch_losses, as.numeric(loss$item()))
    }
    train_pred <- predict_mlp_23(model, X)
    train_brier <- weighted_mean_23((train_pred - y)^2, w)
    held_brier <- NA_real_
    if (!is.null(X_holdout)) {
      held_pred <- predict_mlp_23(model, X_holdout)
      held_brier <- weighted_mean_23((held_pred - y_holdout)^2, w_holdout)
    }
    history[[epoch]] <- data.table::data.table(
      epoch = epoch, training_weighted_Brier = train_brier,
      holdout_weighted_Brier = held_brier,
      mean_minibatch_BCE = mean(batch_losses))
    if (early_stopping) {
      if (held_brier < best_holdout - 0.00005) {
        best_holdout <- held_brier
        best_epoch <- as.integer(epoch)
        epochs_without_gain <- 0L
      } else {
        epochs_without_gain <- epochs_without_gain + 1L
      }
      if (epochs_without_gain >= patience) break
    }
    if (epoch %% 20L == 0L) {
      cat(sprintf("  epoch %3d | 2023 train Brier %.4f | holdout Brier %s\n",
        epoch, train_brier, ifelse(is.na(held_brier), "—", sprintf("%.4f", held_brier))))
    }
  }
  list(model = model, history = data.table::rbindlist(history, fill = TRUE),
       best_epoch = if (early_stopping) best_epoch else max_epochs,
       best_holdout_Brier = if (early_stopping) best_holdout else NA_real_)
}
```

## 5 — Choose network size and stopping epoch inside 2023

A **single 2023 stratified internal holdout** compares three conservative architectures. It is *not* the 2024 calibration set and never uses 2025. Select by the lowest 2023 holdout weighted Brier score, not by accuracy at an arbitrary threshold. This is a small exploratory search rather than a large hyperparameter optimization.

```{r tune-mlp-2023}
set.seed(2302L)
inner_validation_idx <- unlist(lapply(c(0L, 1L), function(cl) {
  ids <- which(train$FMD == cl)
  sample(ids, size = max(1L, floor(length(ids) * 0.20)))
}), use.names = FALSE)
inner_training_idx <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(train)), inner_validation_idx)
stopifnot(!length(intersect(inner_training_idx, inner_validation_idx)))
stopifnot(length(unique(train$FMD[inner_training_idx])) == 2L)
stopifnot(length(unique(train$FMD[inner_validation_idx])) == 2L)

config_grid <- data.table::data.table(
  configuration = c("Small_32_16", "Medium_64_32", "Regularized_48_16"),
  hidden1 = c(32L, 64L, 48L), hidden2 = c(16L, 32L, 16L),
  dropout = c(0.20, 0.30, 0.35),
  learning_rate = c(0.001, 0.001, 0.0007),
  weight_decay = c(0.005, 0.01, 0.01)
)
# Preprocessing was fitted using 2023-only records (including this holdout):
# do not report the internal holdout Brier as an unbiased final performance estimate.
MAX_EPOCHS <- 160L
PATIENCE <- 18L
cv_rows <- list()
cv_histories <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(config_grid))) {
  cfg <- as.list(config_grid[i])
  cat(sprintf("[TUNING] %d/%d: %s\n", i, nrow(config_grid), cfg$configuration))
  fitted <- fit_mlp_23(
    X = X_train[inner_training_idx, , drop = FALSE],
    y = train$FMD[inner_training_idx], w = train_weights[inner_training_idx],
    config = cfg, max_epochs = MAX_EPOCHS, seed = 2300L + i,
    X_holdout = X_train[inner_validation_idx, , drop = FALSE],
    y_holdout = train$FMD[inner_validation_idx],
    w_holdout = train_weights[inner_validation_idx],
    early_stopping = TRUE, patience = PATIENCE
  )
  cv_rows[[i]] <- data.table::data.table(
    configuration = cfg$configuration,
    best_epoch = fitted$best_epoch,
    holdout_Brier = fitted$best_holdout_Brier,
    training_n = length(inner_training_idx), holdout_n = length(inner_validation_idx))
  h <- data.table::copy(fitted$history)
  h[, configuration := cfg$configuration]
  cv_histories[[i]] <- h
  cat(sprintf("[TUNING RESULT] %s | best epoch %d | Brier %.5f\n",
    cfg$configuration, fitted$best_epoch, fitted$best_holdout_Brier))
  rm(fitted)
  invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
}
tuning_results <- data.table::rbindlist(cv_rows)[order(holdout_Brier)]
tuning_history <- data.table::rbindlist(cv_histories)
write_table_23(tuning_results, "23_2023_mlp_tuning")
write_table_23(tuning_history, "23_2023_mlp_tuning_history")
print(tuning_results)
best_row <- tuning_results[1L]
selected_config <- as.list(config_grid[configuration == best_row$configuration])
selected_epochs <- as.integer(best_row$best_epoch)
stopifnot(selected_epochs >= 1L, is.finite(best_row$holdout_Brier))

p_learning <- ggplot2::ggplot(tuning_history,
  ggplot2::aes(x = epoch, y = holdout_weighted_Brier, color = configuration)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("Small_32_16" = "#319F98",
    "Medium_64_32" = "#AF6D46", "Regularized_48_16" = "#C69A51")) +
  plot_theme_23() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "2023 internal holdout: MLP learning curves",
    subtitle = "Model size and epoch count selected using 2023 only",
    y = "Survey-weighted holdout Brier (lower is better)", x = "Epoch")
write_plot_23(p_learning, "23_2023_tuning_learning_curves")
```

This refit uses all eligible 2023 cases, fixed architecture, and **exactly the number of epochs chosen in the prior 2023-only stage**. The 2024/2025 labels are not used in model fitting. Save the model with `torch_save()` rather than `saveRDS()`, because torch tensors require torch-aware serialization.

```{r final-training-2023}

  plot_theme_23() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Final MLP refit: 2023 training Brier",
                x = "Epoch", y = "Training weighted Brier")
write_plot_23(p_refit, "23_2023_final_training_curve", 9, 5)
```

## 7 — Recalibrate using 2024, then freeze before 2025

Intercept-only calibration shifts overall probability without changing within-model ranking; therefore AUROC is unchanged. The 2024 post-calibration mean is matched to 2024 observed FMD *by construction*. The real descriptive calibration check is 2025.

```{r calibrate-2024}
weighted_roc_23 <- function(y, p, w) {
  stopifnot(length(y) == length(p), length(y) == length(w),
            all(y %in% c(0L, 1L)), all(is.finite(w) & w > 0),
            all(is.finite(p)))
  dt <- data.table::data.table(
    score = as.numeric(p),
    pos = ifelse(y == 1L, w, 0),
    neg = ifelse(y == 0L, w, 0)
  )[, .(pos = sum(pos), neg = sum(neg)), by = score][order(-score)]
  P <- sum(dt$pos); N <- sum(dt$neg)
  if (P <= 0 || N <= 0) stop("ROC requires both classes.")
  coords <- data.table::data.table(FPR = c(0, cumsum(dt$neg)/N),
                                   TPR = c(0, cumsum(dt$pos)/P))
  auc <- sum(diff(coords$FPR) *
               (head(coords$TPR, -1L) + tail(coords$TPR, -1L))/2)
  list(coords = coords, auc = auc)
}
weighted_metrics_23 <- function(y, p, w) {
  data.table::data.table(
    AUROC = weighted_roc_23(y, p, w)$auc,
    Brier = weighted_mean_23((p - y)^2, w),
    observed_prevalence_pct = 100 * weighted_mean_23(y, w),
    mean_predicted_pct = 100 * weighted_mean_23(p, w),
    calibration_error_pp = 100 * (weighted_mean_23(p, w) - weighted_mean_23(y, w))
  )
}
fit_intercept_23 <- function(y, p, w) {
  desired <- weighted_mean_23(y, w)
  fn <- function(b) weighted_mean_23(stats::plogis(stats::qlogis(p) + b), w) - desired
  if (fn(-30) * fn(30) >= 0) stop("Cannot bracket a calibration intercept")
  stats::uniroot(fn, interval = c(-30, 30), tol = 1e-10)$root
}
apply_intercept_23 <- function(p, shift) {
  pmax(1e-6, pmin(1 - 1e-6, stats::plogis(stats::qlogis(p) + shift)))
}
calibration_shift <- fit_intercept_23(valid$FMD, p_2024_raw, valid$RAW_WEIGHT)
p_2024_cal <- apply_intercept_23(p_2024_raw, calibration_shift)
p_2025_cal <- apply_intercept_23(p_2025_raw, calibration_shift)
calibration_audit <- data.table::data.table(
  calibration_year = 2024L, log_odds_intercept_shift = calibration_shift,
  observed_2024_pct = 100 * weighted_mean_23(valid$FMD, valid$RAW_WEIGHT),
  predicted_raw_2024_pct = 100 * weighted_mean_23(p_2024_raw, valid$RAW_WEIGHT),
  predicted_calibrated_2024_pct = 100 * weighted_mean_23(p_2024_cal, valid$RAW_WEIGHT)
)
write_table_23(calibration_audit, "23_2024_calibration_intercept")
saveRDS(list(shift = calibration_shift, fitted_on = 2024L,
             source_md5 = source_checksum),
        file.path(model_dir, "23_2024_calibration.rds"))
print(calibration_audit)
```

## 10 — Classification results at 0.16, 0.20, and 0.50

Cells display **unweighted respondent counts** alongside **row-normalized survey-weighted percentages**. Thresholds 0.16, 0.20, and 0.50 are carried over for comparability only, not proposed as clinical decision boundaries.

```{r confusion-matrices}
cutoffs <- c(0.16, 0.20, 0.50)
cm_parts <- list()
for (cutoff in cutoffs) {
  flagged <- as.integer(p_2025_cal >= cutoff)
  for (actual in 0:1) for (predicted in 0:1) {
    match <- test$FMD == actual & flagged == predicted
    cm_parts[[length(cm_parts) + 1L]] <- data.table::data.table(
      threshold = cutoff, actual = actual, predicted = predicted,
      unweighted_n = sum(match), weighted_n = sum(test$RAW_WEIGHT[match]))
  }
}
cm <- data.table::rbindlist(cm_parts)
cm[, weighted_within_actual_pct := 100 * weighted_n/sum(weighted_n),
   by = .(threshold, actual)]
cm[, actual_label := factor(ifelse(actual == 1L, "Actual FMD", "Actual no FMD"),
  levels = c("Actual no FMD", "Actual FMD"))]
cm[, predicted_label := factor(ifelse(predicted == 1L, "Predicted FMD", "Predicted no FMD"),
  levels = c("Predicted no FMD", "Predicted FMD"))]
cm[, outcome_type := ifelse(actual == predicted,
  ifelse(actual == 1L, "True positive", "True negative"),
  ifelse(actual == 1L, "False negative", "False positive"))]
write_table_23(cm, "23_2025_confusion_matrix_cells")
print(cm)
safe_ratio_23 <- function(a, b) if (b > 0) a / b else NA_real_
classification_summary <- cm[, {
  tp <- weighted_n[actual == 1L & predicted == 1L]
  tn <- weighted_n[actual == 0L & predicted == 0L]
  fp <- weighted_n[actual == 0L & predicted == 1L]
  fn <- weighted_n[actual == 1L & predicted == 0L]
  se <- safe_ratio_23(tp, tp + fn)
  sp <- safe_ratio_23(tn, tn + fp)
  ppv <- safe_ratio_23(tp, tp + fp)
  .(respondents = nrow(test),
    observed_prevalence_pct = 100 * weighted_mean_23(test$FMD, test$RAW_WEIGHT),
    fraction_flagged_pct = 100 * safe_ratio_23(tp + fp, tp + fp + tn + fn),
    sensitivity_pct = 100 * se, specificity_pct = 100 * sp,
    precision_pct = 100 * ppv,
    accuracy_pct = 100 * safe_ratio_23(tp + tn, tp + tn + fp + fn),
    balanced_accuracy_pct = 50 * (se + sp),
    F1_pct = 100 * safe_ratio_23(2 * ppv * se, ppv + se))
}, by = threshold]
write_table_23(classification_summary, "23_2025_classification_metrics")
print(classification_summary)

cm_colors <- c("True positive" = "#69B4AE", "True negative" = "#CDE1DD",
               "False positive" = "#F0D29F", "False negative" = "#E4B09E")
for (cutoff in cutoffs) {
  pd <- cm[threshold == cutoff]
  pp <- ggplot2::ggplot(pd,
      ggplot2::aes(x = predicted_label, y = actual_label, fill = outcome_type)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 2) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%\nn = %s",
      weighted_within_actual_pct,
      format(unweighted_n, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE))),
      color = "#42352D", size = 5, lineheight = 1.4) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = cm_colors) +
    ggplot2::coord_equal() + plot_theme_23() +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank()) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = sprintf("2025 AI/AN MLP confusion matrix | cutoff %.2f", cutoff),
      subtitle = "Survey-weighted percentages within outcome; unweighted counts",
      x = "Predicted category", y = "Reported category", fill = "Classification")
  write_plot_23(pp, sprintf("23_2025_mlp_confusion_cutoff_%02d", round(cutoff*100)), 9, 6.5)
}
```

## 11 — Permutation importance grouped by original predictor

On the **2024 calibration year**, shuffle each predictor group together, holding the final network and its fitted 2024 intercept constant, and measure the increase in weighted Brier score. Grouping all dummy columns prevents falsely treating each one-hot code as an independent predictor. These are *predictive associations, not causal effects*. Correlated predictors can share importance. This is slower than evaluating the MLP once; change `N_PERMUTATIONS` to 1 if needed.

```{r 2024-permutation-importance}
N_PERMUTATIONS <- 3L
set.seed(2345L)
# Recover the column-to-predictor mapping directly from model.matrix attributes.
full_mm <- stats::model.matrix(stats::as.formula("~ ."), data = train_df)
assigned <- attr(full_mm, "assign")
encoded_col_names <- colnames(full_mm)[assigned != 0L]
assigned <- assigned[assigned != 0L]
stopifnot(identical(encoded_col_names, colnames(X_train)))
stopifnot(length(assigned) == ncol(X_valid))
importance_baseline <- weighted_mean_23((p_2024_cal - valid$FMD)^2, valid$RAW_WEIGHT)
imp_rows <- list()
for (j in seq_along(selected_names)) {
  cols <- which(assigned == j)
  if (!length(cols)) next
  for (rep_i in seq_len(N_PERMUTATIONS)) {
    shuffled <- X_valid
    permutation <- sample.int(nrow(shuffled))
    shuffled[, cols] <- X_valid[permutation, cols, drop = FALSE]
    p_shuffled <- apply_intercept_23(predict_mlp_23(mlp_model, shuffled), calibration_shift)
    changed <- weighted_mean_23((p_shuffled - valid$FMD)^2, valid$RAW_WEIGHT)
    imp_rows[[length(imp_rows) + 1L]] <- data.table::data.table(
      predictor = selected_names[[j]], replicate = rep_i,
      Brier_change = changed - importance_baseline)
  }
}
importance_replicates <- data.table::rbindlist(imp_rows)
importance_group <- importance_replicates[, .(
  mean_Brier_increase = mean(Brier_change),
  sd_Brier_increase = stats::sd(Brier_change)), by = predictor][order(-mean_Brier_increase)]
importance_group <- merge(importance_group,
  unique(feature_dictionary[, .(encoded_name, feature, domain)]),
  by.x = "predictor", by.y = "encoded_name", all.x = TRUE)
importance_group <- importance_group[order(-mean_Brier_increase)]
write_table_23(importance_replicates, "23_2024_permutation_importance_replicates")
write_table_23(importance_group, "23_2024_permutation_importance_groups")
print(head(importance_group, 15L))
p_imp <- ggplot2::ggplot(head(importance_group, 12L),
  ggplot2::aes(x = stats::reorder(feature, mean_Brier_increase),
               y = mean_Brier_increase)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#319F98", width = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() + plot_theme_23() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "2024 MLP predictor-group permutation importance",
    subtitle = "Change in weighted Brier from shuffling an entire predictor group",
    x = NULL, y = "Brier increase (greater = stronger reliance)")
write_plot_23(p_imp, "23_2024_mlp_permutation_importance", 10, 6.6)
```

## 13 — Reproducibility and interpretation

```{r manifest-and-conclusions}
manifest <- data.table::data.table(
  setting = c("input_file", "input_md5", "training_year", "calibration_year",
    "test_year", "selected_architecture", "selected_epochs",
    "candidate_predictor_groups", "selected_predictor_groups", "encoded_features",
    "training_n", "calibration_n", "test_n",
    "training_seed", "optimizer", "2025_outcomes_previously_inspected",
    "sampling_uncertainty"),
  value = as.character(c(source_path, source_checksum, 2023L, 2024L, 2025L,
    selected_config$configuration, selected_epochs,
    length(feature_specs), length(selected_specs), ncol(X_train),
    nrow(train), nrow(valid), nrow(test), 2399L,
    "AdamW with survey pseudo-weights",
    "yes: exploratory comparison", "not estimated")))
write_table_23(manifest, "23_run_manifest")
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(output_root, "23_R_session_info.txt"))
cat("[COMPLETE] MLP and charts saved under:", output_root, "\n")
```

### Interpretation checklist

1. **MLP versus random forest/XGBoost:** Did the MLP genuinely improve **2025 AUROC and Brier** on identical respondents? Small differences need paired, survey-design-aware uncertainty assessment.
2. **Training stability:** Are the 2023 training/holdout curves diverging? If so, the model may be overfitting even before 2024/2025.
3. **Calibration:** Did intercept-only adjustment align average probability reasonably in 2025? A strong AUROC does not guarantee reliable individual probabilities.
4. **Comparability:** The same source and response coding are used as Notebooks 21–22; different model classes may still respond to sampling weights differently.
5. **Limits:** 2025 evaluation remains exploratory; FMD and poor physical-health days share a 30-day reference period. No causal claims or prospective risk forecasts follow from these cross-sectional results.
